texts.preamble: M/S Ratnesh Packaging Thru.Surendra ... vs Indore Municipal Corporation on 14 February, 2018 ~1~ High Court Of Madhya Pradesh W.P. No. 16928/2017 Indore, Dated: 14/2/2018
texts.facts: By this writ petition, the petitioner has challenged the impugned notices date 1/9/2017 Annex.P/1 by which the stock of polythene bags of the petitioner has been seized and the sample has been taken. The case of the petitioner is that it is engaged in the business of manufacture and retail sale of plastic bags and that the respondents had visited the petitioner's premises on 8/7/2017 and had sealed it on the basis of mere doubt and suspicion. Thereafter, on 1/9/2017 the notice of seizure was served upon the petitioner against which the petitioner had submitted representation dated 10/10/2017 but no action has been taken till now. According to the petitioner, the entire impugned action of the respondents is contrary to applicable provisions of the Act & rules.
texts.arguments: A reply has been filed by the respondents taking the stand that the petitioner is not a manufacturer but he is only a retailer in plastic products. Further plea has been taken that the petitioner was engaged in trading of carry bags and plastic bags having thickness of less than 50 microns which is not permissible under Rule 4 (d) of the Waste Management Rules, 2016 and that the petitioner has violated the provisions of Madhya Pradesh Jaiv Anaashya Apashishta (Niyantran) Act, ~2~ 2004. Further plea has been raised that on receiving the intimation about storage of huge quantity of prohibited plastic products, the petitioner has taken action of seizing the prohibited goods in terms of the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act and that after the seizure the criminal prosecution of the petitioner will be started where he will have full opportunity to defend himself before the JMFC. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that Shri Gautam Bhatiya, the Food Safety Officer had no authority to issue the seizure notice Annex.P/1 and seize the petitioner's goods. Further plea has been raised that the petitioner's godown has been locked and the respondents are not opening the lock thereof inspite of the representation and that the requisite procedure for seizure has not been followed. As against this, learned counsel for respondents submits M/S Ratnesh Packaging Thru.Surendra ... vs Indore Municipal Corporation on 14 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21949840/ 1 that the concerned Food Safety Officer was the authorized officer in terms of the Act and that the due procedure was followed and since the petitioner was retailing the prohibited item, therefore, action has been taken against him and that the act of the petitioner was an offence within the provisions of the Act, therefore, at the stage of prosecution, the petitioner will have full opportunity to defend himself. He further submits that if the petitioner wants to get the seized item released he is required to approach the JMFC by filing an application for Supurdagi. Under the aforesaid provision, the person empowered by the Central Government is entitled to seize the material. Counsel for the respondents has produced a copy of the notification No. SO 83(E) dated 16/2/1987 issued under Section 10 and notification No. SO 84(E) dated 16/2/1987 under Section 11 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 whereby the Food Inspectors have been notified as the ~4~ empowered authority in terms of Sections 10 and 11 of the Act. Hence, the contention of counsel for the petitioner that the seizure notice has been issued and the seizure has been done by the incompetent authority is found to be devoid of any merit. So far as the issue of following the procedure prescribed in Rule 6 of the Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986 is concerned, learned counsel for the respondents has rightly drawn the attention of this Court to the Panchnama Annex.R/1 filed along with the reply which reveals that the seizure has M/S Ratnesh Packaging Thru.Surendra ... vs Indore Municipal Corporation on 14 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21949840/ 2 been done after following the due procedure. Learned counsel for the petitioner has failed to point out from these Panchnama that any of the requirement of the Rule has not been complied with or any illegality in this regard has been done. This Court in order to ascertain the correct position on the spot, vide order dated 12/1/2018 had appointed Commissioner for spot inspection and the report of the Commissioner reveals that only the godown of the petitioner has been sealed.
